text:
Nina: Observed spike of GPU pod evictions in ap-southeast1 at ~02:10 UTC, ~90 evictions over 20m. Realtime latency rose.
Raj: Looking at metrics: attach latency p95 jumped to ~2.8s on warm nodes, conntrack churn and NVLink retransmits increased.
Priya: Workloads affected? tiny-gang fractional requests and a couple RL eval batches.
Nina: Yes, mostly tiny-gang. They scatter and cause NVLink hot spots on dense racks.
Raj: Short-term mitigation: increase device attach timeout/retries and widen scheduler preempt grace to 25s in region to avoid rapid preempts. Also prefer a warm-node pool for tiny-gang (soft prefer nodeAffinity).
Priya: Add a temporary concurrency quota for tiny-gang launches in that region (24h). Limits autoscaler flood.
Nina: Proposed quick canary changes:
- scheduler.preemption.minPreemptionTimeSeconds = 25
- gpu.attach.timeoutSeconds = 10
- tinyGang.maxConcurrent = 50
Raj: Ops steps to prefer warm pool: label pool and patch controller to prefer pool=gang-isol (soft). No hard taints.
ops-bot: Canary deploy started for scheduler+attach config in ap-southeast1 (id: can-17579). Logs in #eng-platform-deploys.
Priya: Opened CR to add quota and runbook note (CR-4599).
Nina: Monitor evictions, attach latency, NVLink errors, and cost due to resubmits. If stable after 30-60m, roll region-wide.
Raj: Also add alert: attach latency >2s for >5m -> pause aggressive scale-ups and page infra-owner.
Priya: Long term: build job sensitivity metadata for evictionPriority and test soft-affinity packing to reduce cross-rack NVLink pressure.
Nina: Thanks team. Will post short incident summary after canary window.
